Agencies Four to five privately placed Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) are expected to tap the public markets by March 2027 to raise a combined Rs 17,000 crore, as infrastructure developers increasingly turn to this route to mobilise long-term capital and monetise operational assets, investment bankers said. InvITs have already mobilised around Rs 88,000 crore through equity issuances during FY23-FY25, indicating growing investor appetite for infrastructure-backed investment opportunities , according to the Bharat InvITs Association . Among the proposed public offerings, Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust has filed for a potential Rs 6,000-crore IPO as it seeks to convert from a privately placed to a publicly offered InvIT. Investcorp-backed NDR InvIT Trust is also planning to transition into a public InvIT through an issue of up to Rs 750 crore, while KKR and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan (OTPP)-sponsored Vertis Infrastructure Trust is also exploring an IPO. In March, NHAI-sponsored Raajmarg Infra Investment Trust raised Rs 6,000 crore through its IPO. Live Events The growing pipeline of public offerings comes amid an expansion in India's InvIT market, estimated at around Rs 7.5 lakh crore, as infrastructure companies increasingly look at the trust structure to unlock capital from operational assets and fund future expansion . The market is also attracting a wider pool of investors. InvITs had around 6.5 lakh unitholders as of the first quarter of FY27, and over the past 10 years, InvITs have collectively distributed nearly Rs 1 lakh crore to their investors, as per the Bharat InvITs Association. Under SEBI regulations, InvITs are required to distribute at least 90 per cent of their net distributable cash flows to unitholders, making them an attractive investment avenue for investors seeking regular income. The investor base is also gradually broadening, with a growing number of women participating as unitholders, according to brokers and wealth advisers. The sector has received a further boost from the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (SEBI) introduction of a framework for depository receipts, allowing foreign investors to gain exposure to Indian REITs and InvITs through select overseas exchanges. Reliance Brands Ltd (RBL), a subsidiary of the country's leading retailer Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd (RRVL), operates business of global fashion and lifestyle brands in India market through strategic partnerships, brand ownership and retail operations . RBL reported revenue from operations of Rs 3,267.66 crore and a profit of Rs 237.12 crore in FY25, according to financial data accessed through the business intelligence platform Tofler. It manages a diverse and expanding portfolio of international and domestic brands across luxury, bridge-to-luxury, premium, and high-street fashion, as well as F&B, eyewear, home & lifestyle, and toys. "Operating within the discretionary consumption space, the company caters to an affluent customer base in India, estimated at 12-15 million consumers, and has established itself as the partner of choice for leading global brands," said RBL. It entered into master franchise partnerships with contemporary womenswear brands Stella McCartney and MAX&Co, as well as British luxury footwear and accessories brand Kurt Geiger, thereby enhancing its presence across premium fashion segments. The company also expanded into the high-growth athleisure and activewear category through a master franchise partnership with Fabletics, launching a new portfolio vertical and reinforcing its commitment to capturing evolving consumer lifestyle trends. "During the year under review, your company achieved a net turnover of Rs 3,390.89 crore as compared to Rs 3,267.66 crore during last year.
